title: Unauthenticated /health discloses catalog upload root and disk inventory
description: An anonymous caller of GET /health receives the absolute catalog upload filesystem path, a count of catalog images on disk, whether R2 is configured, and Gemini model names. That is more than a liveness probe and maps internal layout used by catalog storage. The handler also walks the upload tree (capped at 200000 files) with no auth.
claimed_root_cause: health() is unauthenticated and serializes upload_root() and _count_catalog_image_files() into HealthResponse, unlike production path redaction used for job input_folder.

trace.description: Anonymous health route with no Depends authentication.
upload_root() resolves backend/data/uploads to an absolute Path.
Handler returns catalog_upload_root=str(root), image file count, r2 flag, and model names to the anonymous client.

evidence.description: catalog_upload_root is the raw absolute path string, not public_job_input_folder.
catalog_image_files_on_disk calls _count_catalog_image_files() on every anonymous request.
HealthResponse includes catalog_upload_root, catalog_image_files_on_disk, and catalog_r2_configured.
public_job_input_folder redacts absolute paths in production for jobs only; health does not call it.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox and parent artifact promotion unavailable

validation_plan.local: In the OS sandbox, TestClient GET /health without Authorization and record that catalog_upload_root is an absolute path and catalog_image_files_on_disk is present.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner compares a liveness probe they already use with the JSON fields returned by their API /health; do not scan production disks beyond that observation.
